subject: Subprocessor custody map & evidence routing for SIG/CAIQ review
content:
From: Sophie Lange <security@vandermeer.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Request: subprocessor custody & evidence routing for SIG3 review

Hi Hannah,

We're kicking off a SIG/CAIQ deep-dive for the Nestor Health procurement team and need a clear custody map for Redwood's critical subprocessors. Specifically we need: 

- a roster of subprocessors (name, service provided, country of operations)
- custody/residency proof for KMS keys and any customer-encrypted artifacts
- ownership for runtime components that touch customer content (KV cache, prefix cache), and where telemetry logs are stored/retained
- short attestation that the list is complete as of date and whether any contracts allow sub-subprocessing

Can you provide the above and indicate which artifacts you can produce (CSV roster, residency diagram, redacted logs, signed attestation)? Target due date from procurement is Wed, 22 Dec.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Lange
Senior Security Manager
Van DerMeer Security
security@vandermeer.com

-----
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lange <security@vandermeer.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 15:10:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor custody & evidence routing for SIG3 review

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to support the SIG/CAIQ review. Proposed approach: 

1) Subprocessor roster CSV (name, service, region, contract owner) — Marissa will pull and validate.
2) Custody/residency artifacts: KMS residency diagram + short note on key lifecycle and who holds wrapping keys.
3) Access matrix and proof points for runtime actors (who can read KV cache/telemetry), plus retention windows for logs.
4) A signed attestation template we can populate and sign for procurement.

Quick question: do you want CAIQ-aligned evidence (section mapping), or a concise packet that the Nestor procurement/security team prefers? If CAIQ mapping is required we may need an additional day.

We'll attach items as they become available.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Compliance Outreach | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai

-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lange <security@vandermeer.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:30:45 -0800
Subject: Fwd: subprocessor roster + initial custody artifacts

Sophie — attaching the roster and the KMS residency diagram as a starting point (see attachments). Highlights: 

- storage: AWS S3 (US-EAST-1) for object store, RedactedBucket for customer artifacts (access controlled via IAM roles)
- kms: primary keys in AWS CloudHSM (customer-key option for Dedicated customers; Redwood-managed keys for hosted tenants). See kms_residency.pdf for separation of duties and HSM residency.
- telemetry: partner 'Sightline' aggregates anonymized telemetry; raw telemetry retention limited to 30 days in US regions, 90 days for EU-resident customers where required.
- runtime caching: KV cache lives on GPU instance local NVMe for ephemeral caching. No persistent customer content is stored beyond session expiry.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster.csv; kms_residency.pdf; subproc_custody_diagram.v1.png (diagram).

If you need a hashed key fingerprint only (no raw metadata), call it out and we can provide that.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Vendor & Risk Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Sophie Lange <security@vandermeer.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 13:45:10 -0800
Subject: Re: subprocessor roster + initial custody artifacts

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups: 

- For the KMS residency PDF: can we get a table listing key aliases, origin (CloudHSM/equivalent), and whether Redwood or customer retains key material? Redacted values are fine, we just need provenance and custody statements.
- For telemetry: do you have a sample retention policy statement we can include in the SIG evidence bundle? The procurement team also asked whether any telemetry vendors have cross-border transfer clauses that would pull EU data out of-region.
- The procurement lead also wants a signed attestation that the roster is complete and an explanation of whether any subprocessors can further subcontract.

Also copying their procurement contact for DocuSign if we need a signature: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nestorhealth.com>.

Best,
Sophie

-----
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lange <security@vandermeer.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nestorhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor custody & evidence routing for SIG3 review

Sophie / Tom — thanks for the clarifying asks. Summary and next steps from Redwood: 

- Deliverables: signed attestation (we will populate the template and seek internal sign-off), a provenance table for keys (alias, origin, custody model), an updated telemetry retention statement with clause notes, and the final roster CSV.
- Timeline: we will upload redacted key provenance table and updated telemetry statement to the shared Drive link by 2026-12-21 COB. The signed attestation will be returned via DocuSign by 2026-12-22.
- Escalation: Logan will lead any KMS technical clarifications; Naomi will own legal/compliance sign-off.
- Logistics: evidence bundle will be delivered to https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB3-subproc-evidence and we'll open a Jira ticket for traceability: SEC-4532.

If it helps, we can do a 30-minute walkthrough the week of Jan 4 to go through the artifacts. Please confirm whether procurement needs CAIQ mapping; if so we will add one business day to the delivery timeline.

Attachments included in this thread: subprocessor_roster.csv, kms_residency.pdf, subproc_custody_diagram.v1.png, signed-attestation-template.docx (template to be signed).

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Compliance Outreach | Redwood Inference
